description.fr-FR: Les trois cahiers de Thérèse tels qu’elle les a écrits, sans les retouches de 1898 : le manuscrit A, « histoire printanière d’une petite fleur blanche » dédiée à Mère Agnès de Jésus (1895), le manuscrit B, écrit pendant sa retraite de septembre 1896 pour sa sœur Marie du Sacré-Cœur, où elle trouve sa vocation dans l’Amour, et le manuscrit C, adressé à Mère Marie de Gonzague en juin 1897, sur la petite voie et la charité fraternelle. Texte authentique de l’édition du Centenaire, d’après les archives du Carmel de Lisieux.
description.en-US: Thérèse's three notebooks as she wrote them, without the 1898 revisions: Manuscript A, the 'springtime story of a little white flower' dedicated to Mother Agnes of Jesus (1895); Manuscript B, written during her retreat of September 1896 for her sister Marie of the Sacred Heart, in which she finds her vocation in Love; and Manuscript C, addressed to Mother Marie de Gonzague in June 1897, on the little way and fraternal charity. The authentic text of the Centenary edition, from the archives of the Carmel of Lisieux.
description.pt-BR: Os três cadernos de Teresinha tal como ela os escreveu, sem os retoques de 1898: o manuscrito A, “história primaveril de uma florzinha branca” dedicada à Madre Inês de Jesus (1895); o manuscrito B, escrito durante o retiro de setembro de 1896 para a irmã Maria do Sagrado Coração, no qual ela encontra a sua vocação no Amor; e o manuscrito C, dirigido à Madre Maria de Gonzaga em junho de 1897, sobre o pequeno caminho e a caridade fraterna. Texto autêntico da edição do Centenário, segundo os arquivos do Carmelo de Lisieux.

sources.edition: Archives du Carmel de Lisieux, transcription of the autographs folio by folio (the Nouvelle Édition du Centenaire text), read from the pages' json-cahiers data for Ms A (ff. 2r–86r), /archive/manuscrit-b/ (ff. 1r–5v) and /archive/manuscrit-c/ (ff. 1r–37r); each folio's facsimile URL is kept in the source file.
sources.description: Thérèse's text only. The editors' apparatus is left out: the 'MANUSCRIT A' label, the dating '(Septembre 1896)' over Ms B, the notes on the order of the leaves ('Ici TH rajoute un feuillet 5 r°/v°', '[4v°, suite]'), the image credits, and the bracketed date corrections in the list of graces at the end of Ms A. Words the editors supply in square brackets where Thérèse left one out are kept, bracketed. The division of Ms A follows Thérèse's own: the three periods of her life before Carmel (A 4r), then Carmel. Checked folio side by folio side against the Carmel's former site on the Wayback Machine (242 of 250 sides; A 85r, 86r, C 22v, 23v, 25v, 26r, 28v and 37r have no usable capture). Taken from that witness where the current site is defective: A 59v (printed twice), C 8r (missing; its verso stood in its place), C 26v (empty), C 27r (cut short); and six dropped or misread words. The date of the Virgin's smile in the list of graces (A 86r) is read from the facsimile: May 1883.
sources.tierEvidence: Thérèse died in 1897; the manuscripts were first published in 1956, so the 25-year right in posthumous works (CPI art. L123-4) ended in 1981. The site states no terms (its mentions légales page is empty, checked 2026-11-01); the 1992 editors' notes and headnotes, which are their own work, are not taken.

sources.edition: The same transcription on the Carmel's former site (archives-carmel-lisieux.fr, now offline), one page per folio side, from the Wayback Machine: the second witness.
